summary: Converts an internal 80-bit extended-precision float, read from the word array a1 (sign+exponent word at byte 0xA, mantissa DWORDs at bytes 0x6 and 0x2, lowest word at byte 0x0), into a 32-bit or 64-bit IEEE-style output written through a2, returning a status code (0 = normal/zero result, 1 = range-exceeded, 2 = underflow/denormal). The exponent is decoded against a 0x3FFF bias and the sign extracted from the 0x8000 bit; the mantissa is normalized, rounded and shifted with the helper routines F_4IntCopy, BitArrayClearBitAndZeroFillSubsequentWords, sub_595304, ArrayOf3ZeroCheck and BigIntegerRightShift, using format-control parameters from the a3 array. The output width is selected by a3[4]: 64 writes two DWORDs (a2[1] = v14, a2[0] = upper mantissa DWORD), 32 writes a single DWORD a2[0] = v14.

local_names.a1: input extended-float payload as a 16-bit word array
local_names.a2: output location for the converted float
local_names.v4: sign/exponent word read from byte 0xA of a1
local_names.v20: working mantissa DWORD (byte 0x6 of a1) during normalization
local_names.v19: saved copy of the mantissa DWORD for restore after rounding
local_names.v21: upper mantissa DWORD (byte 0x2 of a1), written as the high half of a 64-bit output
local_names.v8: final exponent value shifted into the output word
local_names.v14: assembled output DWORD: mantissa | sign | exponent

operations.description: Load the extended-float payload from the input word array a1: v20 = mantissa DWORD at byte 0x6, v5 = mantissa DWORD at byte 0x2, v6 = lowest mantissa word at byte 0x0; keep v21 = v5 and v22 = v6 << 16 for the final assembly.
Decode the sign/exponent word at byte 0xA of a1: v23 = v4 & 0x8000 isolates the sign bit and v7 = (v4 & 0x7FFF) - 0x3FFF yields the exponent minus the 0x3FFF bias.
When v7 == -16383 (the exponent field marks a zero/denormal value) skip the normalization path; otherwise take it.
F_4IntCopy(v19, &v20) saves the working mantissa DWORD into the local array v19 so it can be restored after bit clearing and rounding.

BitArrayClearBitAndZeroFillSubsequentWords(&v20, a3[2]) clears the mantissa bit selected by a3[2] and zero-fills the words below it; a non-zero return increments v7 (rounding carry into the exponent).

Compare the exponent v7 against the format thresholds in a3: v10 = a3[1]; when v7 >= v10 - a3[2] the range-handling branch is taken, otherwise the value is treated as subnormal, sub_595304(&v20) is called and the status becomes 2.

Within the range branch, when v7 > v10 the overflow side is selected; the complementary side (v10 - a3[2] <= v7 <= v10) restores the saved mantissa with F_4IntCopy(&v20, v19), right-shifts it by v11 = v10 - v7 via BigIntegerRightShift, clears the bit at a3[2], right-shifts again by a3[3] + 1, and lands on the status-2 result.

On the overflow side, when v7 >= *a3 (a3[0]) the range-exceeded path is taken: sub_595304(&v20), the top bit of v20 is set, v20 is right-shifted by a3[3], v8 = *a3 + a3[5], and the status becomes 1; when v7 < *a3 the normal-result path is taken: the top bit of v20 is cleared, v8 = v7 + a3[5], v20 is right-shifted by a3[3], and the status becomes 0.
ArrayOf3ZeroCheck(&v20) tests whether the mantissa is all zero: a zero mantissa yields status 0 (output zero), a non-zero mantissa is normalized through sub_595304(&v20) and yields status 2.
Select the returned status code: 0 for normal/zero output, 1 for range-exceeded (exponent reached *a3), 2 for underflow/denormal.

Assemble the output DWORD v14 = v20 | (v23 ? 0x80000000 : 0) | (v8 << (31 - *((byte*)a3 + 12))): mantissa from v20, sign bit from v23, exponent shifted into the position given by byte 12 of the a3 array.
Write the converted value according to a3[4]: when it is 64, store the 64-bit output as a2[1] = v14 and *a2 = v21; when it is 32, store only *a2 = v14.
